heading: Other mechanisms can carry most few-shot task learning
definition: few-shot task learning (as opposed to copying repeated tokens) runs mainly through other heads or mechanisms, so V3 overstates induction heads' role.
summary: Several independent groups find that few-shot task learning—learning a task from a few examples in context—relies mainly on heads or mechanisms other than induction heads under the conditions tested. Ablating (disabling) induction heads still impairs classification and speech tasks, so the conclusion depends on the task, which heads are selected and how they are ablated.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: ? (no checked support). 2502.14010's aggregate rows span 70M–7B, but its exclusion result (arXiv:2502.14010#R3) covers only models above 1B, and its verdict reports similar IH and FV effects at Pythia 70M (limits_scope, from text). After the checks, the Pythia 160M–1B timing results of 2607.27281 and the one-head-per-layer ablations of 2509.22947 at 0.13B–1B are cannot_determine for V6 and no longer count as support. 1-10B: R2 with stated scope limits for zero ablation of attention-identified heads in standard and label-absent classification (2505.18752); ablation of the top 3% prefix-matching heads on synthetic Pattern classification in LLaMA-3.1-8B (attention weights zeroed) and Qwen2.5-7B (2507.07810); output ablation of top prefix-matching heads on text-to-speech ICL in SpiritLM 7B (2604.06356); and top-5 induction-head knockout on Open-MI classification in instruct Qwen2.5-VL-3B, without random-head controls (2601.20796). Supports come from 2502.14010, 2504.03022, 2509.24164 and 2511.05743; challenges from 2505.18752, 2507.07810, 2604.06356 and 2601.20796 (Qwen2.5-VL-3B); limits in Pythia-6.9b (2504.03022). In Llama3-8B, Llama2-7B, Gemma-2B and Gemma-7B, zeroing an equal number of random heads also cuts accuracy (arXiv:2505.18752#r06, arXiv:2505.18752#r12, arXiv:2505.18752#r18, arXiv:2505.18752#r21). 10-100B: R2 with a stated scope limit for classification under zero ablation of attention-identified heads. 2505.18752 challenges standard ICL in Llama2-13B/70B and Llama3-70B, where random-head controls barely move (arXiv:2505.18752#r15, arXiv:2505.18752#r03, arXiv:2505.18752#r09), and label-absent ICL in Llama2-13B, but supports the label-absent setting at 70B; 2509.24164 (Qwen2.5-32B, Yi-34B, figure-only) and 2502.20332 (Llama-3.1 70B, correlational) support. 2505.18752 and 2509.24164 share authors (Hao-Lin Yang, Hakaze Cho, Naoya Inoue), so their supports at this scale count as one group; the only other group here is 2502.20332, whose bearing on V6 is correlational. 2407.07011's InternLM2-20B classification ablations have no V6 verdict and count as coverage only. >100B: no evidence (counts: versions.V6.studies_by_size has no >100B key). Size not stated (toy two-layer models): R0 in each direction (2505.16694 supports; 2503.05631 challenges, in a different task).
suggested_status.reason: counts: versions.V6.verdicts gives supports 12 studies, limits_scope 7, challenges 3. Those totals predate the checker's relabelling of arXiv:2601.20796 and arXiv:2503.05631 from limits_scope to challenges; the checked against items label arXiv:2505.18752, arXiv:2507.07810, arXiv:2604.06356, arXiv:2601.20796 and arXiv:2503.05631 challenges. Rule applied here, a working reading of the README definition of C (a failed replication, or a credible paper arguing it is an artifact), which does not say how condition-specific contrary results count: C needs a failed replication of the supporting protocol or a credible artifact argument; a contrary result under another protocol or condition keeps R2, with that condition stated as a scope limit. Independent reproduction supports R2 under this rule. None of the challenges uses the FV-excluded ablation behind arXiv:2502.14010#R3, and no challenges verdict reason in the pack argues that the supporting results are artifacts. Under the practice that gave V2, V3 and V4 C from one condition-specific result each, V6 would be C; one rule across versions is for Iris to set. FV-excluded induction-head ablation has minimal impact above 1B, whereas FV-head ablation excluding induction heads still impairs few-shot accuracy (arXiv:2502.14010#R3, arXiv:2502.14010#R4). HAPAX training at 1B and 2.8B retains or increases abstractive few-shot accuracy despite reduced induction-head formation (arXiv:2511.05743#R15, arXiv:2511.05743#R16, arXiv:2511.05743#R19, arXiv:2511.05743#R20); its venue and review status are not established in the supplied manuscript. Its limits_scope evidence is lower accuracy under aggressive Thresholded-HAPAX masking at 1B, with reduced supervision as a confound (arXiv:2511.05743#R17, arXiv:2511.05743#R18). Previous-token-head ablation does not establish a limitation of V6. Conversely, standard 8-shot classification accuracy falls sharply under IH ablation in Llama models (arXiv:2505.18752#r01, arXiv:2505.18752#r04, arXiv:2505.18752#r07). Zeroing an equal number of random heads barely moves accuracy in Llama2-70B (80.57% → 79.13%, arXiv:2505.18752#r03), Llama2-13B (74.79% → 73.49%, arXiv:2505.18752#r15) and Llama3-70B (81.09% → 77.89%, arXiv:2505.18752#r09). It also cuts accuracy in Llama3-8B (76.20% → 47.86%, arXiv:2505.18752#r06), Llama2-7B (75.13% → 48.15%, arXiv:2505.18752#r12), Gemma-2B (66.16% → 36.48%, arXiv:2505.18752#r18) and Gemma-7B (79.06% → 40.82%, arXiv:2505.18752#r21), so in those models part of the IH effect may be generic zero-ablation damage. Under the rule above, these results (zero ablation of attention-identified heads, without exclusion) are a stated scope limit on V6, not C. In controlled synthetic classification, top-3% prefix-matching-head ablation in LLaMA-3.1-8B changes Pattern recall, as a fraction, by −0.417 to −0.771 under 5- and 10-shot evaluation, while Non-Pattern recall increases (arXiv:2507.07810#H26, arXiv:2507.07810#H12); Qwen2.5-7B degradation across task types is reported qualitatively (arXiv:2507.07810#X01). These recall results do not establish loss of most aggregate accuracy or test label-absent tasks. arXiv:2407.07011's few-shot classification ablations in Llama-3-8B and InternLM2-20B were moved out of V3 as V6 evidence, but the study has no V6 verdict and is not in the V6 pack; its rows are coverage only and do not enter this level. Head selection, ablation type and the definition of task learning remain unresolved sources of disagreement.
suggested_status.open_questions: (1) A same-model, same-task test in Llama 2/3 at 7–70B that runs both protocols: zero ablation of attention-identified IHs as in arXiv:2505.18752#r04, and FV-excluded mean ablation of prefix-matching IHs as in arXiv:2502.14010#R3, each with an equal-size random-head control (random zeroing already cuts Llama3-8B accuracy, arXiv:2505.18752#r06). If the large accuracy drops vanish under exclusion, R2 gains; if they persist beyond random-head damage under the supporting protocol, that is a failed replication and gives C under the rule in reason. (2) Whether the Pattern-recall declines in arXiv:2507.07810#H26 and arXiv:2507.07810#H12 persist under exclusion, with aggregate accuracy and Non-Pattern recall measured alongside them. (3) Label-absent or abstractive tasks with exclusion ablation at 7–13B. (4) Any result at >100B, or in instruct-tuned text, reasoning or non-transformer models. (5) Whether the task-recognition reading holds when IHs are chosen by synthetic prefix-matching scores. (6) Iris's common rule for when a condition-specific challenge gives C rather than R2 with a stated scope limit; under the practice applied to V2, V3 and V4, this level would become C. (7) A V6 verdict on arXiv:2407.07011's Llama-3-8B and InternLM2-20B classification ablations, which have layer-matched random controls (e.g. arXiv:2407.07011#R38, arXiv:2407.07011#R39); until then they are coverage only. (8) Below 1B, a causal test that identifies the few-shot carriers, since no checked V6 support remains there.

original_result.result: The original paper did not test this claim.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: As patterns were discovered, heads encoding token relations strengthened and scores measuring copying fell.
Pretraining to retrieve information did not significantly shorten learning stalls for regression or parity.
Identity-rule task heads correlated weakly with standard induction scores.
Few-shot learning through abstraction persisted without strong induction heads.
Heads learning tasks differed from induction heads, whose removal mainly impaired recognizing which task was requested.
Meaning-based in-context tasks survived removal of token-copying induction heads in Llama and OLMo models.
Removing one head with high induction scores per layer preserved most of the original few-shot accuracy.
A toy meta-learning model inferred which task was given using circuits that did not copy.
Removing previous-token heads hurt learning with labels absent more than induction-head removal in Llama2-70B and Llama3-70B.
Removing generic induction heads widened Llama-3.2-3B's few-shot classification score gaps between correct and competing labels.
Heads carrying task representations mattered more than induction-only heads for few-shot accuracy above roughly 1B parameters.
Few-shot label learning emerged later than induction mechanisms and remained absent in the 70M-parameter model.
Heavy information masking reduced abstraction accuracy; removing heads attending to previous tokens nearly eliminated it.
Few-shot learning depended on an induction circuit in a minimal attention-only model.
Token-copying induction heads also contributed to meaning-based in-context tasks in Pythia-6.9b.
Few-shot accuracy surviving ablation could still reflect backup induction pathways.
Induction-head ablation impaired few-shot accuracy, with effects resembling function-vector ablation in Pythia 70M.
For tasks combining modalities, removing induction heads erased most of Qwen2.5-VL-3B's few-shot accuracy above chance.
SpiritLM speech learning suffered less from removing text-specific than speech-specific heads attending to the prefix.
Removing induction heads reduced few-shot pattern recall on tasks repeating structure or meaning.
Removing induction heads nearly eliminated classification accuracy, even when the query's label could not be copied.
Removing heads that attend to the prefix substantially impaired SpiritLM's few-shot speech generation.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: A same-model comparison of IH sets chosen by attention on ICL prompts (label-token attention) versus synthetic repeated-token prefix-matching scores, under the same ablation type.
untested.basis: Verdict fix on arXiv:2509.24164#r3 (IHs identified by label-token attention). V6 verdict on arXiv:2601.20796 (identification differs from repeated-token tests; no control). The arXiv:2505.18752 untested line (mean or resample ablation instead of zeroing). No row in the pack compares selection methods within one model.

untested.what: Causal attribution of the main carrier of task learning in many-shot settings.
untested.basis: arXiv:2402.13055#R5 reports 20-shot checkpoint evaluations. The checker additionally identifies behavioral evaluations of well-trained InternLM2-1.8B with up to 100 examples in Appendix E and Figures 13–14. Those evaluations do not establish V6's mechanism. The corrected reading of arXiv:2402.13055#R6, arXiv:2402.13055#R7 and arXiv:2402.13055#R8 is timing correlation, without causal attribution, quantified majority contribution, or demonstrated separation of relation-encoding and conventional induction heads. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation does not stratify coverage by shot count.

wording_issues.phrase: runs mainly through other heads or mechanisms
wording_issues.issue: The 'other' heads are not consistently separated from induction heads. arXiv:2502.14010 needs exclusion to separate them: plain induction ablation hurts more than random (R2), and induction and FV heads have similar effects at Pythia 70M (verdict). arXiv:2504.03022 reports concept/token head overlap in OLMo-2-7b and semantic-task damage from token-head ablation in Pythia-6.9b (r8), directly qualifying V6 without isolating training-data effects. In arXiv:2509.22947, only one selected head per layer is removed; redundant induction pathways are a proposed explanation for residual accuracy, whose carriers remain unresolved (R40–R48). In arXiv:2502.20332, the task-carrying 'symbolic induction heads' correlate with standard prefix-matching scores at r = 0.11 in Llama-3.1 70B on an ABA/ABB identity-rules task (r1).

wording_issues.phrase: few-shot task learning (as opposed to copying repeated tokens)
wording_issues.issue: The tested tasks do not uniformly isolate this distinction: arXiv:2505.18752 tests classification with demonstration labels present or absent, while arXiv:2507.07810 uses repetition-based Pattern tasks. In SpiritLM 7B, arXiv:2604.06356 tests demonstration-based TTS; Core demonstrations and targets have no lexical overlap or semantic similarity, but copying versus task learning is not directly separated. Its weaker text-unique-head ablation effect alone does not determine V6's main carrier (r10). arXiv:2509.24164 separates task recognition from task learning: IH ablation mainly removes task recognition (r3, r4), while separate TL heads carry task learning (r5). In arXiv:2505.18752, label-absent and standard ICL give different V6 verdicts at 70B; these accuracy results do not determine V3's token-index-loss effect.

The cited timing and single-head-per-layer experiments do not quantify a majority contribution by non-induction mechanisms. arXiv:2402.13055's timing correlations neither identify the main carrier nor establish separation from conventional induction heads (R6–R8). In arXiv:2509.22947, zeroing one selected induction-scoring head per layer changes the 10-shot function-probe score by −22.6% in 0.13B Baseline (R37) and −4.9% in 0.13B Induction (R40); residual carriers remain unresolved. Conversely, top-10% IH zero ablation reduces standard 8-shot classification accuracy in Llama3-8B from 76.20% to 0.00% (arXiv:2505.18752 r04). In Qwen2.5-VL-3B Open-MI classification, top-5 IH knockout reduces accuracy, as a fraction, from 0.74 to 0.58 against 0.50 chance, removing about two-thirds of the above-chance benefit (arXiv:2601.20796 r16). These are reversals of V6 in the tested settings; Qwen's proxy head identification and missing random-head controls limit causal specificity.

wording_issues.phrase: so V3 overstates induction heads' role
wording_issues.issue: V3 is defined by loss falling with token index, while most V6 evidence uses few-shot task accuracy. The verdict fix on arXiv:2502.14010#R1 distinguishes these measures; that study reports different relative ablation effects on few-shot accuracy and token-loss difference. arXiv:2410.05448#R41 measures transfer timing without token-index loss: Retrieval pretraining did not significantly shorten target ICL plateaus, but induction heads were unverified and the main carrier remains unresolved. arXiv:2511.05743#R14 measures non-extractive token-loss difference, reported as higher in HAPAX but also statistically indifferent. The checker reads the predicted dependence on strong induction heads as absent for V3 on that measure; R14 does not directly test V6's few-shot task-learning claim.

method_sensitivity.what: Heads are identified from attention patterns or label-token attention on ICL prompts in 2505.18752 and 2509.24164; ablating them removes most classification accuracy (2505.18752, Llama3-8B, r04: 76.20% → 0.00%; 2509.24164 r3, figure-only). The r04 result reverses V6 in this condition; V3's token-index-loss effect is cannot_determine. In 2502.14010, induction scores come from synthetic repeated-token sequences, and with FV heads excluded their ablation is about random above 1B (R3). In 2611.05344, knocking out heads chosen by a generic induction score raised the Llama-3.2-3B margin by about 1 nat (verdict).

method_sensitivity.factor: Excluding heads that score high on both induction and FV
method_sensitivity.what: In 12 models (70M–7B), ablating induction heads without exclusion hurts few-shot accuracy more than random (R2); excluding FV heads makes the effect comparable to random in models above 1B (R3).

method_sensitivity.factor: Whether the answer can be copied from the demonstrations (evaluation format)
method_sensitivity.what: In 2505.18752, IH ablation hurts more than PTH ablation in standard 8-shot ICL across seven models. In label-absent Famous People, PTH ablation hurts more in Llama2-70B and Llama3-70B (verdicts; r23: 57.78% → 37.78% after IH ablation). In 2511.05743, HAPAX vs Vanilla at 1B is 19.5% vs 20.6% under standard 5-shot (R15) but 22.1% vs 15.1% when targets are excluded (R16). In 2507.07810, Non-Pattern recall rises while Pattern recall falls (verdict).

2502.14010: the gap between FV and non-FV induction ablation widens with scale (R4 verdict), and IH and FV effects are similar at Pythia 70M (verdict, text). 2505.18752 label-absent: PTH ablation hurts more at 70B, while IH ablation drops accuracy to 0–6.7% in Llama3-8B, Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B and Gemma-2B (verdicts). 2607.27281: few-shot label induction remains flat through 143k steps at Pythia 70M (R8); onset is approximately 12,400 steps at 160M (R9). These timing measurements show temporal dissociation and insufficiency of induction formation, but do not measure causal carriers or their majority contribution; V6 is cannot_determine from them.

2504.03022: in Pythia-6.9b, token-head ablation also damages semantic tasks, unlike in Llama-2-7b, Llama-3-8b and OLMo-2-7b (r8); its method-sensitivity line notes head-type overlap in OLMo-2-7b. 2507.07810 reports a difference between LLaMA and Qwen in its head-ablation effects (method-sensitivity line).

2507.07810, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Repetition Pattern 5-shot: top 1% ablation gives ∆Recall −0.021, a fraction (H01, cannot_determine), and top 3% gives −0.643 (H02). 2509.22947 ablates one selected induction-scoring head per layer on 10-shot function probes; redundant induction pathways are a proposed explanation for smaller drops under curricula. The carriers of residual accuracy are unresolved: these results neither support nor limit V6's majority-carrier claim. 2509.24164 uses a top 3% threshold and also examines other thresholds.

At 1B, exact-match HAPAX keeps standard 5-shot abstractive accuracy close to Vanilla (19.5% vs 20.6%, R15). Similarity-thresholded masking (τ = 0.3) lowers it to 10.9% (R17). Heavy masking reduces training supervision, confounding attribution of the lower accuracy specifically to induction suppression. These accuracy comparisons concern V6 performance retention: observed for R15 and partial for R17. They do not measure V3's token-index-loss effect.

In 2507.07810 (LLaMA-3.1-8B, top 3% head ablation, 5-shot ∆Recall as a fraction), structural tasks drop more (Repetition −0.643, Recursion −0.721) than semantic ones (WordSeq 1 −0.417, WordSeq 2 −0.453). In 2504.03022, Llama-2-7b nonsense copying fails after token-head ablation (r3) while semantic tasks survive (verdict). In 2604.06356, SpiritLM 7B is evaluated on demonstration-based TTS using a prefix-matching identification proxy; copying versus semantic or abstract task learning is not directly compared. Its less pronounced degradation under text-unique head ablation does not separately establish V6 or identify the main task-learning carrier.

status_amendment.public_note: The overall rating stays at independently reproduced (R2), and at 10–100B parameters it changes from contested to R2, because contrary results from other methods or tasks are now counted as limits on where the claim holds rather than as failed replications; under the stricter practice used for some other versions it would be contested, and one rule for all versions is still to be set. Below 1B parameters, outside toy models, the rating is now undetermined, and in four of the smaller models removing the same number of random heads also cuts accuracy sharply, so part of the damage in the main contrary study may not be specific to induction heads.
